content.title: 5 Places to Watch a Spurs Game
content.text: The Block SA This UTSA-area food truck park has three large flatscreens under its covered bar where fans can enjoy the game. Beer, liquor and cocktails are available from the bar while several food trucks—including Bull Gogi Boys, Clutch City Cluckers and Golden Street Taco GDL—mean there’s a variety of options on any given day. 14530 Roadrunner Way Cover 3 When you want gametime food that’s elevated, this restaurant delivers. Its San Antonio and Austin locations have become hot spots for game watching parties thanks to a plethora of TVs, a fan-friendly atmosphere and an extensive menu that features everything from mahi mahi tacos to buffalo chicken sliders and flatbreads. 1806 N. Loop 1604 W. Freetail Brewing Co. Brewpub The menu here is so extensive you may have to keep snacking throughout the game. Start with Freetail nachos before moving on to a handcrafted pizza or specialty sandwich or salad. There are also 10-plus beers on tap, wine and other drinks. TVs are situated throughout the pub and there’s a large screen on the far wall so you can see the game from any table. 4035 N. Loop 1604, Ste. 105 The Friendly Spot Fans can watch the game on Slab Cinema’s inflatable outdoor big screen at this Southtown beer garden. With 76 taps and 300-plus bottles and cans, there’s a drink for everyone. The menu includes nachos and other snacks, and there’s even a playground for kids who don’t want to sit through the game. 943 S. Alamo St. Smoke BBQ + Skybar The location of the Spurs organization’s first official watch party, this downtown venue is family friendly, has plenty of screens on which to see the game and has a full menu of ‘cue and drinks. On Oct. 21, the Spurs will also bring DJ Quake, the Spurs Hype Squad and in-arena host Zay Zay. We hear there may even be a chance to win autographed basketballs and future home game tickets. 501 E. Crockett St.
